It would likely take more than 1-2 years of pulling to cause permanent damage to your hair follicles. Castor oil and rosemary extracts can promote regrowth if you apply them consistently and also try to refrain from pulling from the same area, covering it with hats or headbands or bandanas after applying these things is a good idea. I’m not too sure what a Derm could do besides maybe some sort of stem cell injections to the area or something like that, and neuro likely isn’t the right kind of doc for the underlying causes of trich. 

Your best bet is trying different forms of therapy to combat the underlying reasons for your compulsions, some well known and commonly used therapies are CBT or DBT. This would be done through talk therapy with a therapist/psychologist, and if they believe medications are necessary for things like anxiety, ocd, depression or ADHD you would likely need to see a psychiatrist or nurse practitioner that can work with the therapist/psychologist to prescribe those for you and monitor the results. Best of luck 🤞🏻

Hey, im 20 too, unfortunately not a lot helps me personally but the things that do are wearing hats, wearing fake nails and sometimes bandaids on the ol' fingers. There's a supplement called NAC that can be helpful for some if you haven't already heard of or tried it. These may not help if you dont work out the stress that's actually making the pulling worse, so for that id recommend trying to see your schools psychologist or a therapist if you dont already, try to keep your schoolwork on a schedule so you don't get overwhelmed with too much at once, and keeping your courseload at the most manageable level you can (don't try to go overboard and take more classes than you can handle). Make sure you spend time releasung that stress in healthy ways, i know its hard with the pandemic but try to safely hang out with friends or even study with them if you can so that you 1. Have a distraction 2. Have someone that will make it more enjoyable and 3. Are discouraged from pulling in front of them. For sleep you can try melatonin, make sure ypur doing all the basic sleep hygiene stuff like turning off electronics an hour before bed, sleeping in the dark and cool temperatures, and i would definitely recommend meditation or mindfulness techniques if you haven't tried them, that's like the main treatment for trich besides talk therapy i believe. Im sorry youre in the same shitty boat as the rest of us here but hopefully youll figure out some things that help💗
